Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions
Sponsor: Gray
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 04/13/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 609 as introduced would allow the Alabama Innovation Corporation, created by House Bill 540 to (1) make matching grants of up to $250,000 to entities that have received a federal Small Business Innovation Research grant or a federal Small Business Technology Transfer Research grant and (2) set guidelines and priorities for awarding these matching grants.
Howard Sanderford, Chair
Boards, Agencies and Commissions

Committee: Healthcare
Sponsor: Shaver
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 04/06/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 237 as passed the House of Representatives could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the Board of Pardons and Paroles and the Department of Corrections by an amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and penalties imposed.
Jim McClendon, Chairperson
Healthcare

Date: 02/24/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 237 as amended and reported by the Committee on Judiciary could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the Board of Pardons and Paroles and the Department of Corrections by an amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and penalties imposed.

Judiciary

Committee: Health
Sponsor: Shelnutt
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 03/16/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 10 as amended and reported by the Committee on Health could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, local jails, the district attorneys, the Department of Corrections, community corrections programs and the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Additionally, this bill could decrease the obligations of Alabama's Medicaid Program by an undetermined amount dependent on (1) the number of minors who would have otherwise been provided treatments or services prohibited in the bill and (2) the cost to the Program for these treatments or services.
Paul W. Lee, Chair
Health
